parametric-functions-s1.title: The path of $f(t) = (t^2 - 4, t^3 - 4t)$
parametric-functions-s1.text: The path is traced for $-2.5 \le t \le 2.5$. Arrows show the direction of travel as $t$ increases.

table.caption: Position of a drone at selected times: x(t) is meters east of the launch pad and y(t) is meters north of it

items.q: Use the formula for $f$. At which point is the path when $t = 1$?

why.correct: $x(1) = (1)^2 - 4 = -3$ and $y(1) = (1)^3 - 4(1) = -3$, so the point is $(-3, -3)$, below the $x$-axis on the loop.
options: Both coordinates come from $t = 1$: $x(1) = -3$ and $y(1) = -3$.
This is the point for $t = -1$, where $y(-1) = -1 + 4 = 3$.
$x(1) = 1 - 4 = -3$; the sign of $t^2$ was flipped to get $-5$.

items.q: The path goes through the origin twice. For which values of the parameter is the point at the origin?
options: Just $t = 0$

why.correct: At the origin both coordinates are $0$. $x(t) = t^2 - 4 = 0$ gives $t = -2$ or $t = 2$, and $y(-2) = -8 + 8 = 0$, $y(2) = 8 - 8 = 0$. Both work.
options: Both $t = -2$ and $t = 2$ make $x(t) = 0$ and $y(t) = 0$.
At $t = 0$ the point is $(-4, 0)$, the left end of the loop.
$t = 0$ is extra: $x(0) = -4$, so the point is $(-4, 0)$ then.
$x(0) = -4$, so $t = 0$ gives $(-4, 0)$, not the origin.

items.q: As $t$ increases through $0$, the point passes $(-4, 0)$. Which way is it moving there?
options: Down, from $(-3, 3)$ toward $(-3, -3)$
Up, from $(-3, -3)$ toward $(-3, 3)$
Left, away from the origin along the $x$-axis
Right, back toward the origin along the $x$-axis

why.correct: Just before $t = 0$ the point is near $(-3, 3)$ (at $t = -1$) and just after it is near $(-3, -3)$ (at $t = 1$). The arrows on the loop point down at $(-4, 0)$.
options: From $t = -1$ to $t = 1$ the point goes from $(-3, 3)$ to $(-3, -3)$: downward.
This reverses the order; $(-3, 3)$ comes first because $-1 < 1$.
$(-4, 0)$ is the leftmost point: $x(t) = t^2 - 4$ is smallest at $t = 0$, so the point turns from moving left to moving right there.
The point is turning around in $x$ at $(-4, 0)$; its clear motion there is downward.

items.q: Why is this path not the graph of a function $y = g(x)$?
options: At $t = -1$ and $t = 1$, $x = -3$ but $y$ is $3$ and $-3$: one $x$, two $y$-values
It crosses itself at the origin, which the graph of a function of $x$ does not do
The $x$-coordinates are negative for $-2 < t < 2$
$y(t) = t^3 - 4t$ is a cubic in $t$, so $y$ is not a function of $x$

why.correct: A function of $x$ gives one $y$ for each $x$. Here $x(-1) = x(1) = -3$ while $y(-1) = 3$ and $y(1) = -3$, so $x = -3$ has two $y$-values.
options: Specific values settle it: $x = -3$ comes with $y = 3$ and $y = -3$.
Passing the same point twice gives one $y$ for that $x$, which a function allows. The problem is an $x$ with two different $y$-values.
Negative $x$-values are fine for a function; the issue is two outputs for one input.
Cubics in $t$ can trace graphs of functions of $x$, for example $(t, t^3)$. Use specific points instead.

items.q: For which values of $t$ in $[-2.5, 2.5]$ is the point moving to the left?

why.correct: The point moves left where $x(t) = t^2 - 4$ is decreasing. A parabola opening up decreases to the left of its vertex, so $x$ decreases for $-2.5 < t < 0$ and increases after.
options: $x(t) = t^2 - 4$ falls from $2.25$ to $-4$ as $t$ goes from $-2.5$ to $0$.
For $t > 0$, $x(t)$ increases, so the point moves right.
This is when the point is on the loop; it moves left for half of that time and right for the other half.
The point keeps moving left after $t = -2$, all the way to $t = 0$.

items.q: Where is the drone at $t = 3$ seconds?

why.correct: Read both rows in the column $t = 3$: $x(3) = 5$ and $y(3) = 7$. The point is $(x(3), y(3)) = (5, 7)$, 5 meters east and 7 meters north.
options: The coordinates are swapped; $x$ comes first.
$4$ is $y(2)$, from the wrong column.
$3$ is the time, not a coordinate.

items.q: Between which two readings does the drone first move west?
options: Between $t = 2$ and $t = 3$
Between $t = 1$ and $t = 2$
Between $t = 3$ and $t = 4$
Between $t = 0$ and $t = 1$

why.correct: West means $x$ decreases. $x$ goes $2, 5, 6, 5, 2$: it first falls from $6$ to $5$, between $t = 2$ and $t = 3$.
options: $x$ drops from $6$ to $5$ here: the first move west.
$x$ rises from $5$ to $6$ here, so the drone moves east.
The drone does move west here, but it already did between $t = 2$ and $t = 3$.
$x$ rises from $2$ to $5$, so this move is east.

items.q: The drone is at $x = 5$ at two different times. What does that tell you?
options: At $x = 5$ the heights are $2$ and $7$, so the path is not the graph of a function of $x$
The drone was at one and the same point at $t = 1$ and again at $t = 3$
The drone hovered in place from $t = 1$ to $t = 3$ before it moved west
$x(t)$ is not a function of $t$, since two times share the output $5$

why.correct: At $t = 1$ the drone is at $(5, 2)$ and at $t = 3$ at $(5, 7)$: one $x$-value, two $y$-values. The path in the $xy$-plane fails to be the graph of a function of $x$, while $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ are still functions of $t$.
options: $(5, 2)$ and $(5, 7)$ share $x = 5$ with different $y$.
The $y$-values differ ($2$ and $7$), so they are different points.
The drone went east to $x = 6$ and back; it did not stay put.
Each $t$ has one $x(t)$, so $x(t)$ is a function of $t$; repeated outputs are allowed.

items.q: How many meters north does the drone move from $t = 1$ to $t = 4$?

mistakes.why: That is the change in time, $4 - 1$. North is the $y$-row: $11 - 2 = 9$.

items.q: In a parametric function $f(t) = (x(t), y(t))$, what does the parameter $t$ do?
options: Each value of $t$ picks out one point $(x(t), y(t))$
$t$ is the slope of the curve at the point it produces
$t$ is the $x$-coordinate of each point
$t$ is the distance from the origin

why.correct: The parameter is the input: each $t$ gives one point, and increasing $t$ sets the order of the points.
options: $t$ goes in, the point $(x(t), y(t))$ comes out.
A slope compares changes in $y$ and $x$; $t$ is the input that produces both.
The $x$-coordinate is $x(t)$, which usually differs from $t$.
The distance from the origin is $\sqrt{x(t)^2 + y(t)^2}$, not $t$.

items.q: A curve is given by $x(t) = 2t + 1$ and $y(t) = t^2$. Write $y$ as a function of $x$.

mistakes.why: This puts $x(t)$ inside $y$. Solve for $t$ first, $t = \frac{x - 1}{2}$, then square it.

items.q: A curve is given by $x(t) = 3 - t$ and $y(t) = t^2 + 1$. What is $y$ at the point where the curve crosses the $y$-axis?

mistakes.why: That is $y(0)$. On the $y$-axis $x = 0$, so $3 - t = 0$ and $t = 3$.
$t = 3$ is the parameter value; the question asks for $y(3) = 3^2 + 1$.

items.q: Compare $g(t) = (t, t^2)$ for $0 \le t \le 2$ with $h(s) = (2s, 4s^2)$ for $0 \le s \le 1$. Which statement is true?
options: Both trace $y = x^2$ from $(0, 0)$ to $(2, 4)$, in the same direction
$h$ traces the parabola $y = 4x^2$, a different curve
$h$ traces the same parabola in the opposite direction
$g$ and $h$ are both at $(1, 1)$ when the parameter is $1$

why.correct: For $h$, $x = 2s$ and $y = 4s^2 = (2s)^2 = x^2$. As $s$ goes from $0$ to $1$, $x$ goes from $0$ to $2$, the same points and the same direction as $g$.
options: Both give $y = x^2$ for $0 \le x \le 2$, starting at $(0, 0)$.
$4s^2 = (2s)^2 = x^2$, so the parabola is $y = x^2$.
Both start at $(0, 0)$ and end at $(2, 4)$, so they go the same way.

items.q: Put the steps for sketching a parametric curve in order.
options: Choose several values of $t$ in the interval
Compute $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ for each value
Plot each point $(x(t), y(t))$
Join the points in order of increasing $t$ and add arrows

why.correct: Values of $t$ first, then the coordinates, then the points, then the curve joined in the order the parameter gives, with arrows for the direction.

items.q: A curve $f(t) = (x(t), y(t))$ is changed to $g(t) = (x(t) + 2, y(t))$. Predict each change.

variables.name: The $x$-coordinate of the point for each $t$
variables.why: Every $x$-coordinate gains 2, so the whole curve slides 2 units right.

variables.name: The $y$-coordinate of the point for each $t$
variables.why: $y(t)$ is unchanged, so every point keeps its height.

variables.name: The number of times the curve crosses itself
variables.why: A slide moves every point the same way, so crossings stay crossings and no new ones appear.

why.correct: Adding 2 to $x(t)$ shifts the curve right by 2 and changes nothing else.

items.q: Which function traces the same path as $f(t) = (t, t^2)$, $-1 \le t \le 2$, but in the opposite direction?
options: $(-t, t^2)$ for $-2 \le t \le 1$
$(t, -t^2)$ for $-1 \le t \le 2$
$(-t, t^2)$ for $-1 \le t \le 2$
$(t^2, t)$ for $-1 \le t \le 2$

why.correct: For $(-t, t^2)$, $y = t^2 = (-t)^2 = x^2$. With $-2 \le t \le 1$, $x = -t$ runs from $2$ down to $-1$, so the path goes from $(2, 4)$ to $(-1, 1)$: the same points, backward.
options: It starts at $(2, 4)$ and ends at $(-1, 1)$, the reverse of $f$.
$y = -x^2$ is the parabola reflected across the $x$-axis, a different path.
With $-1 \le t \le 2$, $x = -t$ runs from $1$ to $-2$: a different piece of the parabola.
Swapping the coordinates gives $x = y^2$, a parabola opening right.
